stance: Universal temporal progression is postulated to be consistent everywhere; gravity, motion and environmental conditions can affect physical processes, not progression itself under the premise. No independently established absolute clock or simultaneity mechanism is claimed.
charter: Time does not physically exist; it is the “When.”

dinner.limitation: Universal progression and the reunion schedule are stipulated. Rates are illustrative independent inputs, not derived from gravity, velocity, or biology. No travel dynamics, remote synchronization or biological aging law is solved. The home deadline is operationally defined by a reference clock; both relativity and this model allow reunion with different accumulated clock readings.

parameters.label: Candidate multiplier of published relativistic gradient

benchmark.limitation: The multiplier is a freely stipulated comparison, not an ArcSecs-derived prediction. Published statistical and systematic uncertainties are combined in quadrature solely as an illustrative scale assuming independence; the residual is not a p-value, a new fit, or a test of universal time itself. The sign follows the authors’ reported gradient convention.

observations.title: Optical clocks and relativity
observations.summary: Aluminum-ion optical clock comparisons resolved gravitational frequency differences for a 33 cm change in elevation, and motion-related frequency changes. This record supplies context, not a digitized measurement series.

observations.title: Resolving the gravitational redshift across a millimetre-scale atomic sample
observations.summary: A frequency gradient was resolved within an ultracold strontium ensemble. The reported fractional frequency measurement uncertainty reached 7.6 × 10⁻²¹; this is a precision figure, not the measured gradient.

observations.title: A lab-based test of the gravitational redshift with a miniature clock network
observations.summary: The authors report a signed gradient of −12.4 ± 0.7 (statistical) ± 2.5 (systematic), in units of 10⁻¹⁹/cm, with a relativistic reference of −10.9 in the same units.

additionalCalculations.scope: Separate conditional educational controls; original dinner and benchmark API remains unchanged.
